evidence.quote: I have discovered that improved results may be obtained in carrying out reactions in the gas eous phase in the presence of a catalyst consist ing of a reduction product of a fused mixture of
if there is incorporated in Said catalysts one or more of the elements magnesi um, aluminum, chromium, zirconium, vanadium, titanium, thorium, silicon and cerium.

props.name: superior activity, better physical form, less consumption, smoother operation

evidence.quote: by providing new catalysts of superior activity and improved physical form, decreasing catalyst consumption and improving Smoothness of oper ation,

props.statement: The new catalysts provide superior activity and improved physical form, decrease catalyst consumption and improve smoothness of operation.

props.name: avoid iron, nickel and cobalt in catalyst and gases

evidence.quote: it is recommended that Suitable precautions be taken for avoiding the presence of metals of the iron group (iron, nickel, and cobalt) in the catalyst and in the gases that are to react.

props.statement: In synthesizing methanol, precautions should be taken to avoid metals of the iron group (iron, nickel and cobalt) in the catalyst and in the reacting gases.

props.name: above 200 atm methanol condenses almost completely with water cooling

evidence.quote: example, at pressures above 200. atmospheres to practically completely condense methanol from the gases by cooling with water at ordinary tem perature.

props.statement: In methanol synthesis at pressures above 200 atmospheres methanol can be practically completely condensed from the gases by cooling with water at ordinary temperature.

props.name: more CO: more vigorous reaction, heat must be removed to avoid damage and methanation

evidence.quote: If the gaseous mixtures contain relatively higher pro portions of carbon monoxide, the reaction pro ceeds more vigorously, greater quantities of heat are evolved
so that the catalysts may not be damaged by over heating and undesirable side reactions, such as methanation, may be avoided.

props.statement: With higher carbon monoxide proportions the reaction proceeds more vigorously and evolves more heat, which must be dissipated so that the catalysts are not damaged by overheating and side reactions such as methanation are avoided.

props.name: gases with only 3-15% CO can be used

evidence.quote: tures containing hydrogen and carbon monoxide in which the proportion of the latter is relatively low, for example, between 3 and 15%.

props.statement: The catalysts are not limited to any gas composition; methanol can be synthesized from hydrogen-carbon monoxide mixtures with relatively little carbon monoxide, for example between 3 and 15%.

props.name: catalysts with two or more of the elements with Cu and Mn also suitable

these elements. Such catalysts have the desir able characteristics hereinbefore mentioned

props.statement: A catalyst containing two or more of the mentioned elements in combination with copper and manganese can be prepared similarly and has the same desirable characteristics.

props.name: preferred methanol synthesis: 400-1000 atm, 250-500 C

evidence.quote: I prefer to carry out the synthesis of methanol at a pressure within the range of 400 to 1000 at mospheres and at a temperature of 250° to 500° C.

props.scope: pressure 400 to 1000 atmospheres; temperature 250 to 500 C
props.statement: The methanol synthesis may be conducted at various pressures and temperatures but is preferably carried out at 400 to 1000 atmospheres and 250 to 500 C.

props.name: gas passed over the catalyst in a pressure receptacle; product condensed

evidence.quote: the prepared catalyst is disposed in a suitable receptacle adapt ed to withstand the pressure at which the re 55 action is conducted.
The gaseous mixture containing the product of the reaction is withdrawn and cooled to effect Condensation of the product

props.statement: The catalyst is placed in a receptacle withstanding the reaction pressure; the gas is introduced at the proper temperature, and the product-containing gas is withdrawn and cooled to condense the product.

props.name: gases must be freed of sulphur compounds

evidence.quote: the gases should, nevertheless, be freed from impurities which are likely to deleteriously affect the catalyst, and of these the compounds of sulphur are the most commonly encountered.
The Sulphur compounds may be removed pre 70 75 liminarily from the gases by suitable treatment

props.statement: The gases should be freed from impurities likely to deleteriously affect the catalyst, of which sulphur compounds are the most common; they may be removed beforehand by the usual treatment.

props.name: reduction is exothermic and must be slow

evidence.quote: Since the reduction process is exothermicit should becarried out slowly, and with care so that the catalyst may not be damaged by excessive temperature.

props.statement: Since the reduction is exothermic it should be carried out slowly and with care so that the catalyst is not damaged by excessive temperature.

props.name: activity superior to fused Cu-Mn oxide alone and to the added elements alone

evidence.quote: The catalysts herein described exhibit an ac tivity superior to that of a catalyst consisting of fused and reduced copper oxide and manganese. oxide alone; and also superior to that of any of the foregoing list of elements taken singly or in combination with each other.

props.statement: The catalysts exhibit an activity superior to that of fused and reduced copper oxide and manganese oxide alone, and to that of any of the listed elements singly or in combination with each other.

props.name: definition of 'superior activity'

evidence.quote: The term "superior activity' is used to indicate that with a given rate of gas flow the catalysts give a higher yield of product per hour or, correspondingly, to at tain a given hourly production a lower rate of gas flow may be maintained.

props.statement: 'Superior activity' means a higher yield of product per hour at a given gas flow rate, or a lower gas flow rate for a given hourly production.

props.statement: In some cases the reduction may yield a lower and especially active oxide that, together with the activated copper, forms a mass especially suited to catalytic production of oxygenated hydrocarbons; the patentee offers no theory for composition changes.
